news.title: 5 unique aspects of the 2026 U17 World Cup.
news.lede: TPO - World youth football is focusing all its attention on Doha, Qatar, which is preparing to host the FIFA U17 World Cup 2026 (taking place from November 19th to December 13th). This tournament has some quite special details, differing significantly from other major FIFA events. Here are 5 of the most special things.

news.title: Son Heung-min happy to see back of ‘disappointing’ year with South Korea
news.lede: South Korea's Son Heung-min has vowed to come back stronger in 2027 after a disappointing year for his national side. SEOUL – Son Heung-min said South Korea had suffered “a lot of disappointing moments” in a turbulent year that included an early World Cup exit and bitter internal divisions in the team. South Korea beat Qatar 1-0 in a friendly in Doha on Nov 17 to end an annus horribilis for Son and his international teammates, who were dumped out of the World Cup in the group stage after a shock loss to South Africa. Unpopular coach Hong Myung-bo quit in the wake of their early exit, before reports emerged of a split involving the 34-year-old Son and some of the other players, including Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae.

news.title: Nike Ditches Men’s Kit Templates With New ‘Fenom’ Tech for 2027 Women’s World Cup
news.lede: 2027 Women’s World Cup, Football Kits, Nike. Nike has pulled back the curtain on the technology it hopes will define the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup. In a week where they returned as the ball manufacturers for UEFA, Nike has gone on to further restablish themselves in the heart of the footballing world with their new, state-of-the-art technology. The brand has previewed ‘Fenom’, a head-to-toe performance apparel system designed for the tournament in Brazil, aimed at improving cooling, support, and focus for female players.

news.title: Soccer-Moriyasu leaves mixed legacy as loss ends era for Japanese football
news.lede: Nov 18 (Reuters) - Hajime Moriyasu brought ⁠the curtain down on his eight years in charge of Japan in Singapore on Tuesday hoping that he ⁠has laid the groundwork for the country to eventually win the World Cup. The 58-year-old had signed a ‌contract extension after the World Cup in North America that would have taken him through to the end of the Asian Cup in February. However, the postponement of that event until December 2027 means Moriyasu's time at the helm ended this week. "I believe the key is for Japan to continue building on ​its current strength in order to become the best team in the ⁠world," he told Nippon TV after side's 2-1 ⁠defeat by Paraguay in his 113th match as Japan coach.

news.title: Soccer-Tashima confirms backing of five national federations, submits bid for FIFA presidency
news.lede: TOKYO/BANGKOK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Japan Football Association (JFA) ⁠Honorary President Kozo Tashima said on Wednesday he has submitted his candidacy for the FIFA presidency after securing the support of five national federations. Nominations for the ⁠FIFA presidential election close at 2259 GMT on Wednesday, four months before the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat on March 18, where the vote ‌will take place. Gianni Infantino is seeking reelection for a fourth term as head of global soccer's ruling body. Candidates need at least five member associations to nominate them.

news.title: Boycotts, bans and no-shows: Notable World Cup absentees
news.lede: The first World Cup was hosted by Uruguay in 1930 and featured 13 teams, just four of which were from Europe: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. The paucity of European teams wasn't due to a boycott but largely had to do with funds being short during the Great Depression and the difficulty of traveling such a long distance by sea. It would be linked to a boycott at the next World Cup. Italy both hosted and won their first World Cup in 1934.

news.title: Temporary coach says he is ready to help develop national football team if given chance
news.lede: Robert Moreno, who was brought in to handle six friendly matches following the FIFA World Cup, said that Korean football has the potential to move in a good direction but did not discuss his contract, which expires on Nov. 27, in more detail. After winning what could have been his final match with Korea in Doha, Qatar, on Tuesday, Robert Moreno, the national football team’s interim head coach, said that he is ready to help the country improve if given the chance. Korea edged out Qatar 1-0 at Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium in their last friendly match of the year. This marked Moreno’s final match under his contract’s terms.
